Read and Answer.main_question: Read the passage and answer the questions
Read and Answer.passage: Zara lived near a big farm. Every morning, she woke up early and fed the hens. One day, she saw a small duckling alone near the pond. It was cold and shaking. Zara wrapped it in her warm scarf and carried it home. She gave it some water and soft bread. Her brother Omar made a cosy bed from a box. By evening, the duckling was warm and happy. The next day, they took it back to its mother. The mother duck quacked loudly in thanks. Zara smiled. She felt proud of helping.

points.text: Correct place: near a big farm

scheme.common_error: Says she lived near a pond.

questions.question: What did Zara feed every morning?

scheme.common_error: Says she fed the duckling.

questions.question: Who made a cosy bed from a box?

scheme.common_error: Says Zara made the bed.

questions.question: What did Zara give the duckling to eat and drink?
questions.answer: She gave it water and soft bread.

scheme.common_error: Names only one item.

questions.question: Why did Zara wrap the duckling in her scarf?
questions.answer: The duckling was cold and shaking, so the scarf kept it warm.

accept: To make it warm because it was shivering
scheme.common_error: Says Zara wanted a pet.

questions.question: How did the duckling feel by evening?

scheme.common_error: Says it was still cold.

questions.question: Why did the mother duck quack loudly?
questions.answer: She was thankful that her duckling was back safe.

accept: To say thank you to the children
scheme.common_error: Says she was angry.

questions.question: Why did Zara feel proud at the end?
questions.answer: She had helped a little duckling in need.

accept: Because she was kind and saved the duckling
scheme.common_error: Says she was proud of her scarf.

questions.question: Zara had not wrapped the duckling in the scarf. What would have happened to it?
questions.answer: It would have stayed cold and shaking and could have been unwell.

points.text: It would be unhappy or unwell

accept: It would keep shivering and feel sad
scheme.common_error: Says the duckling would be warm anyway.

questions.question: Why was it good that Zara took the duckling back to its mother?
questions.answer: The duckling belonged with its mother, who was waiting for it.

points.text: Mother would miss or need it

accept: So the mother duck would not be sad and the duckling would be safe
scheme.common_error: Says Zara did not want to keep it.

slots.instruction_en: Read the passage and answer the questions.
slots.prompt_rule: One new passage of 80 to 110 words in "passage", on a book theme, in Grade 2 words. "questions": ten objects { question, answer, marks: 2, scheme } — four recall, four understand, two apply — where scheme.points sum to 2. Every question is answered from the passage: the two apply questions ask the child to use what the passage says (why, or what would happen if), never to write about themselves and never a grammar or tense change (no "Write one sentence about", no "Change this sentence"). Do not prefix a question with a letter.
Three book words. Answer: a model sentence; accept any correct sentence using the word.

Three book words. Answer: one rhyme; accept lists other real rhymes. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the given word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture and write the word.
slots.prompt_rule: Two book objects as picture: {kind:"object", name}. Answer: the word. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.
Three sentences with one blank; options exactly is, am, are.

Three book words with one or two letters blank, one underscore for each missing letter ("b__k" for book, "man_o" for mango); the picture is the clue. Answer: the full word. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the answer word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.
Three book adjectives or verbs. Answer: the opposite.

Three book nouns (one -es, one irregular). Answer: the plural. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the given noun, one of it, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.
Three sentences with one blank; options exactly has, have.

slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture. Write in, on, under, near or behind.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items, each a scene as picture: {kind:"scene", describe} of one object placed by another (a cat under a table), placed in, on, under, near or behind it, never above, over, beside or next to. The describe names the floor and the thing's own legs or base ("a ball on the floor under a chair", "a bird on top of the roof"). Never a bird or animal in or on a tree, or in any scene where both in and on read true (a bird among the leaves of a branch is both): use in only for a thing inside a container (box, basket, bag, cup). Stem: "The cat is ____ the table." Answer: that one word. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Write the sentence again. Use he, she, it or they.
slots.prompt_rule: Four sentences naming a person or thing; the child writes each sentence again with the pronoun. Answer: the full rewritten sentence with the pronoun in place of the name, e.g. "He is playing outside." Scheme: A 1 for the correct pronoun in the rewritten sentence.
Topic exactly "My House". Answer: a model paragraph of five sentences. Scheme: five K points of 2 — on topic, five sentences, capitals and full stops, spelling, describing words.
Three nouns with a blank before them; options exactly a, an.

slots.instruction_en: Put a full stop (.) or question mark (?).
slots.prompt_rule: Three short sentences with no end mark, each a statement or a question, never an exclamation. Answer: the sentence with its . or ?.

slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture and write three sentences.
slots.prompt_rule: One busy scene from a book theme (a park, a market, a classroom) as picture: {kind:"scene", describe}. Answer: three model sentences. Scheme: three K points of 2 — each a correct sentence about the picture. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Put the sentences in order to make a story.
slots.prompt_rule: One short story of six sentences from a book theme, given out of order and listed in "questions" as plain sentences with no number or letter in front (the paper letters them (a)-(f)). Answer: the order. Scheme: one K point of 1 per sentence in the right place. Write the story so exactly one order is valid; if two orders are really valid, list every valid order in scheme.accept.

content.script: Pinky and Jojo found a shiny door in their school. Out stepped three people who looked confused. One was Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah. One was Sufi Tabassum, and one was Shabana Akhtar. Pinky and Jojo told each person a story about their life. Then a shiny door opened for each of them, and they went back home. Pinky and Jojo felt proud because they had helped their new friends.

items.ask: What did Pinky and Jojo find in their school?
Which three people stepped out of the door?
items.answer: Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, Sufi Tabassum and Shabana Akhtar stepped out.

items.ask: How did Pinky and Jojo feel at the end of the story?
What happened after Pinky and Jojo told each person a story about their life?
items.answer: A shiny door opened for each of them, and they went back home.

items.ask: Think about your own life. Who is a person you look up to, and why?
items.answer: Any sensible answer, for example: I look up to my teacher because she is kind and helps me.

items.ask: Today, please talk about your best friend. What is your best friend's name?
What do you like to do together with your best friend?
Why do you like your best friend?

content.script: Pinky said to Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, "You are known as the mother of our nation. You worked hard for our country Pakistan and helped women get their rights." Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah smiled and said, "Yes, I remember now!" A shiny door opened, and she walked through.

items.ask: Pinky said to Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, "You are known as the mother of our nation.
You worked hard for our country Pakistan and helped women get their rights."

A shiny door opened, and she walked through.
